account:
It is day 1, just after 07:00. I am in the town hall reading today's appointments. The confirmed schedule has me in the office at 08:00, inspecting grain at the east-bank mill at 10:00, home for lunch at noon, back for council letters at 13:00, taking tea with the neighbour at the cottage at 15:00, and returning to the office at 16:30. There is also an approved great hall lighting inspection at 18:00 with the builder and secretary. The secretary deposited its signed addendum last evening; I have taken it out but have not yet read it.

The hall's eight new lanterns and the builder's inspection are the clearest recent town business I know about. The builder is waiting near the hall this morning. As far as I know, the lights are intended to make the hall welcoming in the evenings, not for any confirmed special occasion.

There are a few things I do not yet understand. Yesterday the neighbour mentioned vague talk of a bridge or port change, but could not confirm it, and the secretary said no such proposal had reached the office. This morning I heard freight ask the innkeeper to discuss today's freight arrangements at the inn. That may simply be ordinary business; I have no evidence connecting it to the river rumours or the lighting. Several nearby conversations were indistinct, so I cannot infer their contents.

The town accounts papers were still unlocated yesterday, leaving receipts and outstanding payments unverified. The secretary reported a balance of 128 emeralds, but that is not an audited account. I want to learn what business is actually underway without treating rumours as facts. My original appointment book remains authoritative; the secretary's other appointment book was only a provisional record, not proof of a changed schedule.
